skill_drafts.name: Decorator-Based Observability Instrumentation
skill_drafts.description: Apply Python decorators (@workflow, @agent, @operation) to functions and classes to automatically capture execution spans and observability data with minimal code overhead.
skill_drafts.objective: Enable observability instrumentation of agent workflows and operations
contraindications: Real-time streaming contexts where decorator overhead is prohibitive
workflow_steps: Apply @workflow decorator to workflow function or @agent to agent class
Apply @operation decorator to operation methods within agent class
Ensure decorator nesting follows proper span hierarchy
Execute decorated code; spans are automatically emitted
triggers: Developer needs to add observability to a workflow function
Agent class requires execution span capture
constraints: Decorators must be applied in correct hierarchy: @agent wraps class, @operation wraps methods, @workflow wraps functions
output_contract: Decorated function or class that automatically emits execution spans to observability backend; no manual span creation required

metadata.prompt: Use @workflow decorator on workflow functions, @agent on agent classes, and @operation on operation methods. Nest decorators to establish proper span hierarchy. Each decorator automatically emits execution spans to the observability backend without additional instrumentation code.
metadata.section_summary: Add powerful observability to your agents, tools, and functions with as little code as possible: one line at a time.

skill_drafts.name: Nested Span Hierarchy Management
skill_drafts.description: Compose multiple decorators (@agent, @operation) in proper nesting order to establish correct parent-child span relationships and execution context hierarchy in observability instrumentation.
skill_drafts.objective: Maintain correct span hierarchy in nested agent and operation contexts
applicable_signals: Nested method calls within agent classes
Need for parent-child span relationship tracking
contraindications: Flat, non-nested function calls without hierarchical context requirements
Contexts where span hierarchy is not required for observability analysis
Standalone functions that do not require parent-child span relationships
intervention_moves: Apply @agent decorator to the class definition
Apply @operation decorator to individual methods within the class
Verify decorator nesting order matches execution hierarchy
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Identify the class definition that represents the agent', 'detail': 'Locate the class that contains the operations to be instrumented'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Apply @agent decorator to the class definition', 'detail': 'Place @agent decorator immediately before the class keyword'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Apply @operation decorator to each method requiring observability', 'detail': 'Place @operation decorator immediately before each method definition within the class'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Verify span hierarchy in observability output', 'detail': 'Confirm that operation spans appear as children of the agent span in observability logs or traces'}
triggers: Adding observability to nested method calls within agent classes
Establishing parent-child span relationships for hierarchical execution tracking
constraints: Decorators must be applied in correct nesting order: @agent on class, @operation on methods
Parent decorator (@agent) must wrap the class before child decorators (@operation) are applied to methods
Execution context must support decorator composition
cautions: Incorrect decorator order will result in flat span structure instead of hierarchical relationships
Missing decorators on nested methods will break span hierarchy chain
Verify observability output to confirm parent-child span relationships are established
output_contract: Properly nested decorators that produce correct parent-child span relationships in observability output, with operation spans registered as children of agent spans.

examples.input: Class-based agent with multiple methods that need observability tracking
examples.output: @agent decorator on class, @operation decorators on methods, resulting in hierarchical span structure
examples.notes: Operation spans are correctly nested under agent span in observability output

metadata.prompt: When instrumenting class methods or nested function calls, apply decorators in the correct nesting order: place @agent on the class definition and @operation on individual methods. This ensures that operation spans are correctly registered as children of the agent span, preserving the execution context hierarchy for observability analysis.
